findings.message: All result_contract=2 schema-version checks are removed from SPEC-1 through SPEC-8; a v1 result that happens to include the newly checked top-level fields (test_output, run_mode, exit_code) will pass every SPEC assertion without ever proving the schema version contract is enforced.

SPEC-7 reversal: the prior assertion explicitly required exit_code to be absent at top level (enforcing data encapsulation under data.{}); the replacement now requires it at top level, silently widening the information surface exposed to downstream consumers without a guard that the data.exit_code path is still present on error paths.

SPEC-8 combines an unrelated field-presence check (test_output at top level) with the signal-death mapping assertion using pipe-delimited string concatenation; a failure in either half produces an opaque mismatch string that cannot distinguish which invariant broke, masking regressions.

SPEC-3 and SPEC-4 each emit two assert_eq calls sharing the same tag string ([SPEC-3], [SPEC-4]); test harnesses that match on tag to count or report failures will attribute both failures to the same spec, obscuring whether the exit_code or disposition invariant broke.

SPEC-11 in the fallback writer test drops the result_contract=2 version check and replaces it with run_mode=full; run_mode can equal 'full' on a v1 or otherwise malformed result, so this no longer guards the v2 calling convention it claims to verify.
